## Historical audit: S0263

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_4/results/task01/reference/H_start/selection/commons_31294395/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines and supplied character ranges.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — student request, line 1 [0,11554) | Reconstruct a single 512×341 indoor photograph as separate SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, placement and materials. The student’s inventory interprets it as a historic bedroom; that interpretation is not independent image verification. |
| First build — student response and execute, lines 3 [0,14148), 4 [0,14808) | A complete program created multiple named assets: room, two windows, portraits, bed, chairs, screen, furniture and rugs. It included child parts such as bed rails and chair arms, procedural wallpaper, glazing emission, a camera and lights. Named hierarchy and coordinates show intended membership and placement, not verified physical connections or image fidelity. |
| First validation — execution result and next request, lines 5 [0,39466), 6 [0,58), 7 [0,65431) | Step 1 returned `ok: true`, saved a render and was selected. The next student request included the reference and render paths and asked for comparison or DONE. The images themselves are not visible in this audit. |
| Autonomous revision — student response and execute, lines 9 [0,14601), 10 [0,15261) | The student reported too much ceiling, undersized foreground furniture, a misplaced frontal chair and excessive brightness. These are student observations, not independently verified findings. The executed revision moved and turned the chair, widened the bed and added a rectangular bedding core, changed camera position and aim, reduced world and area lighting, and changed wallpaper shading and other details. This was a substantive revision, not an empty patch. |
| Final visible result — execution result and select, lines 11 [0,40703), 12 [0,59) | Step 2 returned `ok: true`, saved a render and was selected. No subsequent comparison, DONE response, score or independent geometric validation appears in the supplied trace. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update or student receipt/adoption is recorded. The comparison instruction and rendered image were runner feedback, not a teacher intervention. The student independently produced and revised the scene; the recorded CLI sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2 [0,2889), 8 [0,3373)).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** The observed outcome is **successful execution and selection of a revised build**, with semantic reconstruction quality unknown—not established formal success, algorithm failure or technical interruption. Multiple objects, materials, part membership, chair pose and camera/light settings are evidenced in code, but actual visual coverage, part contact, occlusion, pose accuracy, texture fidelity and remaining camera or lighting defects cannot be checked without the images. Whether the second render improved the first remains unresolved.

**Lessons.** Transferably, a render-and-revise cycle can separate an executable build from claims of visual correctness; successful rendering alone proves neither. Task-specific hypotheses about ceiling, chair placement and brightness motivated the particular changes, but their diagnoses and effectiveness remain unverified.
